verdict.rationale: ReadMe documents a per-project MCP server that gives AI assistants like Cursor, Claude Code and VS Code Copilot a live connection to the project's API spec and documentation. Its MCP analytics record each tool call along with the query behind it, which implies agents can run search queries against the published docs. Missing for 10: an explicit list of the search and page-content tools the server exposes, and independent or hands-on confirmation that agents can query it.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my published docs site exposes its own MCP server that my users' agents can query for search and page content

citations.quote: Your MCP server gives AI coding assistants — Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code Copilot — a live connection to your API spec and documentation.
Every time an AI client calls a tool on your project's MCP server, ReadMe records the call.
The MCP page in Analytics shows how many calls arrived, how quickly they returned, how many failed, and the query or endpoint behind each call.
